Œuvres du domaine public au Met (Open Access, CC0), aucune déjà postée ce mois-ci. Faits vérifiés : Canaletto, Piazza San Marco (fin des années 1720) : vues vendues aux voyageurs du Grand Tour (anglais surtout). Guardi, Venise vue du bassin de Saint-Marc (vers 1765-75) : jugé de son vivant inférieur à Canaletto ; touche rapide. Degas, Vue de Saint-Valéry-sur-Somme (1896-98) : un de ses derniers paysages, vue déclinante. Slide Artura : version `cta A`, son logo sous le paragraphe, jamais une capture. Couverture : une vraie photo de musée de la banque de l'OS (id dans `banque`), jamais d'image IA. en.titre: Paintings That Make Me Want To Travel

en.texte: is Venice in the late 1720s, sunlit and almost too perfect. Canaletto painted it for rich young travelers on their Grand Tour, who wanted to bring Venice home with them.

en.titre: Venice from the Bacino di San Marco
en.texte: is the same city seen by Francesco Guardi: looser, mistier, alive. In his lifetime he was considered a lesser Canaletto. I learned to see how his gondoliers are made of a few quick flicks of paint on Artura, one artwork a day with its story.
is one of the last paintings Degas made, in the late 1890s, when his eyesight was failing. The little town by the sea dissolves into patches of color.
